clips.send: Climax. The turning point: the moment of highest tension. After the climax, the story can’t go back to how it was. Della opens Jim’s gift: combs — for hair she no longer has. This is situational irony: the opposite of what we expect.

clips.send: Falling action. Loose ends get tied up. Tension drops. We learn the results of the climax. Jim reveals he sold his watch to buy the combs. Chinese classes often fold this into the ending (结局).

clips.send: Rising action (1). Complications pile up. Tension climbs. Usually the longest part of a story. Each event makes the problem harder or the stakes higher. Della sells her hair: now there’s no going back.
clips.text: Rising action (1). Complications pile up. Tension climbs. Usually the longest part of a story. Each event makes the problem harder or the stakes higher. Della sells her hair: now there’s no going back.

clips.send: Rising action (2). Even more pressure, right before the peak. Writers often slow down here to build suspense. Della waits by the door, whispering a prayer. Ask: what could go wrong now?

clips.send: Exposition. Meet the characters, the setting and the problem. Answers: who? where? when? what’s wrong? In “The Gift of the Magi”: a small New York flat, Christmas Eve, only $1.87. Often ends with the inciting incident — the spark that starts the trouble.

clips.send: Resolution. The new normal. The conflict is settled. Shows how the characters (or the world) changed. O. Henry’s narrator calls the couple “the wisest” — “They are the magi.” The resolution often points straight at the theme.

clips.send: 易错点：上升情节通常有好几个事件，而不只一个。

clips.send: 发展（上升情节 1）。困难一个接一个，紧张度上升。 通常是故事最长的部分。 每个事件都让问题更难，或让代价更高。 黛拉卖掉了头发——再也回不了头了。

clips.send: 结局。新的平静，冲突解决了。 展示人物（或世界）发生了什么变化。 欧·亨利的叙述者说这对夫妻是“最聪明的”——“他们就是麦琪。” 结局常常直接指向主题。

clips.send: 易错点：紧张的时刻不一定就是高潮——高潮是转折点。
clips.text: 易错点：紧张的时刻不一定就是高潮——高潮是转折点。

clips.send: 下降情节。解开剩下的结，紧张度下降。 我们看到高潮带来的结果。 吉姆说出：他卖了表，才买了梳子。 语文课上常把这一部分并入“结局”。

clips.send: 易错点：开端不是“高潮前的所有内容”，只是铺垫部分。
clips.text: 易错点：开端不是“高潮前的所有内容”，只是铺垫部分。

clips.send: 开端（背景介绍）。介绍人物、环境和问题。 回答：谁？在哪里？什么时候？出了什么问题？ 《麦琪的礼物》：纽约一套小公寓，圣诞前夜，只有 1.87 美元。 结尾常有“激发事件”——点燃麻烦的那个火花。

clips.send: 高潮。转折点：紧张度最高的时刻。 高潮过后，故事再也回不到原样。 黛拉打开吉姆的礼物：梳子——可她已经没有长发了。 这是情境反讽：结果和我们的预期正好相反。

clips.send: 发展（上升情节 2）。高潮前，压力更大。 作者常在这里放慢节奏，制造悬念。 黛拉守在门边，小声祈祷。 问问自己：现在可能出什么岔子？
